Re: Public Records Act Request

Dear Alpine Community Planning Group Members,

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I am writing to request a copy of the records detailed below.

I am researching how the Alpine Community Planning Group (ACPG) conducts its business on the part of the residents of Alpine in preparation for publication of an expose. To that end, I request the following records:

1. All Alpine Community Planning Group Agendas and Minutes from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025.

2. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and another member(s) of the Alpine Community Planning Group from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

3. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and another government agency, including between the group members and the County of San Diego from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

4. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and any member of the public, including between the group members and individuals/entities with business before the group from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

Please note that the Public Records Act allows a member of the public to request records by describing their content, rather than asking for specific documents by name; an agency that receives such a request must “search for records based on criteria set forth in the search request.”

Public records represent “any handwriting, typewriting, printing, photostating, photographing, photocopying, transmitting by electronic mail or facsimile, and every other means of recording upon any tangible thing any form of communication or representation, including letters, words, pictures, sounds, or symbols, or combinations thereof, and any record thereby created, regardless of the manner in which the record has been stored.” (Government Code section 7920.545.)

1. This request applies to all records in your agency’s possession, including documents created by a member of another government agency or a member of the public.

2. If specific portions of any documents are exempt from disclosure, please provide the non-exempt portions.

3. Please provide entire documents, even if only parts of them are responsive to this request.

If you maintain records or data in electronic format, please provide them in that same format.

1 California First Amendment Coalition v. Superior Court, 67 Cal.App.4th 159, 165-66 (1998).
2 See California State University v. Superior Court, 90 Cal. App. 4th 810, 824-25 (1999).
3 Gov’t. Code § 6253(a). versions are acceptable) to avoid copying costs.
4 If you are unable to reproduce electronic records in electronic form, please provide a reason for doing so.

I request that you waive copying fees because I have limited resources, and the information requested will be used in the public interest to further the public’s understanding of the local community planning group action. None of the information obtained will be sold or distributed for profit. If you are unable to waive the copying fees, and you anticipate that these costs will exceed $50, or that the time needed to copy the records will delay their release, please contact me so that we can arrange to inspect the document or decide which documents we wish to have copied. Otherwise, please copy and send them as soon as possible. Please respond to this request within ten (10) days, either by providing all the requested records or by providing a written response setting forth the legal authority for withholding or redacting any document and stating when the documents will be made available.

If you require any clarification in identifying responsive documents or focusing this request, please contact [redacted]. Please send all records responsive to this request to Louis Russo.

Thank you for your time and attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

[redacted]

emails.body:
Thank you for this good report…but it made me wonder, as many things do, about the “bikeway” move.  The questions here are pertinent because there are real constraints on bicycle use.  First, the rider has to be reasonably fit; those of us who are aged, infirm, or handicapped are much less likely to use bicycles—or to be able to use bicycles.  Then the rider has to be close enough to the workplace to make commuting by bike feasible…AND to have access that doesn’t include freeways.  That leaves almost all of us in the County out.  Finally, there needs to be a place to change into office clothes (assuming these are still worn) at the workplace.  Also time and perhaps a place to keep office clothes.

And there is a limit to what can be carried on a bike.  The week’s grocery shopping on the way home?  Other shopping errands?  Not likely.  How much work related material can be hauled?

The bottom line is that it’s possible the whole “bikeway” move in the city will only end up making life more difficult for the majority of us who don’t or can’t use bicycles.

Subject: Report on SANDAG's July Meetings to the Association of Planning Groups - San Diego County

Good Morning APG Members,

Note: At the July 26, 2024 SANDAG Board of Directors meeting there was no (zero) County representation. This means we had no one representing the Unincorporated Area with the power to vote. Nora Vargas was absent. Joel Anderson was absent. The County Board of Supervisors has two alternates: Terra Lawson-Remer and Monica Montgomery Steppe. Neither were present. When a vote was taken to consider borrowing $20 million of future Transnet funds for the "Transnet Regional Bike Early Action Program" there was no one from the County to vote. We had an empty seat.

SANDAG's CEO, Mario Orso:

Mario Orso reported that SANDAG would continue to provide updates to the Board and stakeholders on the priority corridors of SR 78 and SR 67. He did not include SRs 76, 79 or 94 in this priority list. The Transnet Independent Taxpayer Oversight Committee is seeking community members for their Board. Information located at their website: https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/transnet-independent-taxpayer-oversight

SANDAG will not hold Board of Director meetings in August, but staff and working groups will continue with work.

APG comment to Board: This month we held the first Evacuation Tour with SANDAG and Caltrans staff. The potential evacuation routes in the Ramona area were thoroughly explored and wildfire hazards such as chimney fire burn zones were identified for the group by our local fire behavior expert, Dan Summers. The next Evacuation Tour will explore the SR 94 corridor from Campo to Jamul; including the dangerous intersection of Otay Lakes and Honey Springs Road. The Unincorporated Community values these opportunities to partner with SANDAG and Caltrans to share vital boots-on-the-ground knowledge in order to develop safe evacuation routes for all travelers in the region. Thank you.

California Transportation Commission (CTC):

Two CTC Commissioners introduced themselves and reported that they are "the money people" for State and Federal transportation funds. Commissioners Clarissa Reyes Falcon and Lee Ann Eager invited Board members to attend an upcoming meeting being held in San Diego from August 15-16. Website for information:

https://catc.ca.gov/meetings-events/commission-meetings-2024

Transnet Oversight Annual Report and Performance Audit and Budget:

The overall feedback from the Board to those presenting on Transnet funds and projects was that there was a clear lack of information and accountability is needed. Cost Benefit Analysis was missing. Staff reported miniscule use of the public transportation options and utilization of biking or walking - Return On Investment is dismal. SANDAG often quotes the maxim that limited funds should be used to help the most people. Historically, the Transnet funds are benefitting very few. As of FY 2023, total bikeway Program funding was $397.3 million. Transnet funds represented $187.2 million (47%) of this spending. The promise of the Transnet funds to improve public safety through corridor projects is not being met. SANDAG staff's explanation was that the voters had an expectation and the funding sources for these projects (of which Transnet funds are only one part/source) come with stipulations that are often in conflict with what the voters expected. This is the difficult environment in which planning and funding for projects exists.

emails.subject: Park Fee Changes Starting February 18, 2025
emails.body:
Hi Travis,

At the County of San Diego Parks and Recreation Department, we take great pride in maintaining beautiful, safe, and accessible outdoor spaces for everyone to enjoy. To continue providing high-quality parks, trails, and recreation services, we will be making some adjustments to our park service fees starting February 18, 2025.
This is our first fee update in nearly 11 years, and while we’ve worked hard to keep costs as low as possible, this change is necessary to help offset rising maintenance and operating expenses. The updates also align our fees with similar parks and facilities in the region while ensuring that we continue to deliver best-in-nation outdoor experiences.

What’s Changing?
Most of the fee increases are just a few dollars, but they will help us keep our parks safe, clean, and well-maintained for generations to come. Here are a few examples of the adjustments:

  *   Day Use Parking: Increasing from $3.00 to $5.00 per day
  *   RV Partial Hook-Up Campsite: Increasing from $29 to $35 per night
  *   Camping Reservations: Now include up to two pets and one extra vehicle at no additional cost
  *   Other small increases apply to rentals, permits, and additional park services

To see the full list of updated fees, please visit our 2025_DPR_User_Fee_Changes_01.17.25.pdf<https://www.sdparks.org/content/dam/sdparks/en/pdf/public-meetings/fee_increase/2025_DPR_User_Fee_Changes_01.17.25.pdf>. For more information on why these changes are happening, check out our FAQs_Park User Fee Increase 01.17.25.pdf<https://www.sdparks.org/content/dam/sdparks/en/pdf/public-meetings/fee_increase/FAQs_Park%20User%20Fee%20Increase%2001.17.25.pdf>.

Why Are Fees Increasing?
The cost of maintaining our 158 parks, 389 miles of trails, and over 58,000 acres of land has risen significantly over the past decade. Adjusting our fees will allow us to:
✔ Continue offering high-quality park experiences and amenities
✔ Keep trails, facilities, and green spaces safe and well-maintained
✔ Expand and improve park programs and services for all ages and abilities
Even with these updates, our park fees remain affordable and continue to offer exceptional value compared to similar park systems.

Ensuring Parks Remain Accessible for Everyone
We believe that everyone should have access to nature—which is why we continue to offer financial assistance programs and free or low-cost activities:
🌿 Discounted Programs: Veterans, seniors, and groups may qualify for discounts on fees and reservations.
🏕 First-Time Camping Program: A free initiative designed to introduce new campers to the joys of the outdoors.
🎉 Low-Cost or Free Activities: Most of our recreation programs and events are available at reduced or no cost.
We are committed to making the outdoors accessible and enjoyable for all members of our community.

Thank You for Your Support!
We appreciate your understanding and continued support as we make these necessary updates. Your visits, participation, and enthusiasm help keep our parks vibrant and welcoming for everyone.
If you have any questions or would like more details, please visit our Fees Increase Feb. 18<https://www.sdparks.org/content/sdparks/en/news-events/news-stories/Fees-Increase-Feb-18.html>.

We look forward to seeing you at the parks!

Thanks & Go Aztecs,

emails.body:
[County of San Diego]
There is still time to apply for the first phase of the Cannabis Social Equity Program! 

This application period closes on August 23rd at 11:59 pm. There will be opportunities to apply for future application periods. The next one will open in late 2024. 

The application<https://equity.projectcannabis.org/> will help determine if you meet the program’s eligibility requirements. All applicants who meet the requirements will be contacted by the County.

Those who qualify will receive various benefits.  These include expungement assistance, and one-on-one mentoring, training – workshops, webinars, and classes to help program participants prepare for the opportunity to open a cannabis business in the unincorporated area of the county. 

This application cycle also includes a grant lottery.  Ten awardees will be selected on September 18th.  Additional future grant opportunities may be available depending on funding. 

Currently, new cannabis licensing is not permitted in the unincorporated county but is estimated to begin in Winter 2025.

To review the eligibility criteria and apply please visit:
Cannabis Equity Eligibility Application (projectcannabis.org)<https://equity.projectcannabis.org/>

More Program Information
Stay informed by visiting the Engage San Diego Socially Equitable Cannabis Program Hub<https://engage.sandiegocounty.gov/hub-page/cannabis-program>.

Questions
Have questions about the program?
For questions about the Social Equity Program, contact Brandon Lewis, Social Equity Manager, at brandon.lewis@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:brandon.lewis@sdcounty.ca.gov>. 

For questions about the County’s Cannabis Licensing, Enforcement, Ordinances and Environmental Impact Report contact pds.longrangeplanning@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:pds.longrangeplanning@sdcounty.ca.gov>.

Informational Sessions
Future informational sessions for the Cannabis Social Equity Program will be held in-person. Click here for more details, request language services, and let us know if you plan to attend.

From: Othering & Belonging Institute
To: Lewis, Brandon
Subject: [External] End the siege and starvation of Gaza
Date: Wednesday, July 30, 2025 10:16:30 AM
July 30, 2025
Black image with bold text reading, 'Stop Starving Gaza'
We, the undersigned, are writing to express our horror and outrage at
Israel's forced starvation and ceaseless bombings of Gaza.

We have all seen images of emaciated children being intentionally
starved, families crushed or burned alive in airstrikes, and heard
the desperate cries of parents pleading for the world to end their
immeasurable suffering. We have all witnessed countless acts of
unconscionable cruelty, including Israeli forces killing more than 1,000
Palestinians since May while trying to collect a bag of flour or rice from
aid distribution sites to bring back to their starving families.

With the UN secretary general warning that Gaza's “last lifelines
keeping people alive are collapsing,” and the World Health
Organization declaring Gaza's remaining hospitals to be at a "breaking
point," it is crucial for the international community to put
forth concrete steps to end Israel's U.S.-backed genocide in Gaza.

We demand an immediate ceasefire in Gaza, as well as the lifting of
the siege, and the resumption of aid deliveries to nourish and treat the
starving, ill, and wounded Palestinians who have been subjected to a
nearly complete blockade of food, medicine, and other vital supplies
since March. This blocking of food and medicine is not only immoral, it
is also a war crime under the Geneva Conventions.

We add our voices to the global outcry demanding that the killing and
forced starvation be stopped immediately, that the death traps run by
the so-called Gaza Humanitarian Foundation be dismantled,
and for the United Nations to resume the distribution of that aid, as
“only a massive scale-up in food aid can stabilize the hunger
catastrophe engulfing Gaza.”

What we are witnessing in Gaza is a stain on our collective conscience,
and we all have a responsibility to do something to end it. We invite
people from all institutions, wherever you may be located, to sign
onto this letter, or use it as a template to create your own.

Signed,

Institute, UC Berkeley
- Denise Herd, Associate Director, Othering & Belonging Institute, UC

Item: 4. NOTICED PUBLIC HEARING: HARMONY GROVE VILLAGE SOUTH GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT, SPECIFIC PLAN, ZONE RECLASSIFICATION, TENTATIVE MAP, MAJOR USE PERMIT, SITE PLAN AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT AND ASSOCIATED DOCUMENTS

eComment: To Board I suggest approval of Harmony Grove Village South. I won't go into the obvious reasons thousands of people have been saying, 'we need more housing'. That is a given. As a former Planning Commissioner and City Council member in the City of Escondido I am very familiar with the time consuming procedures and processes to get approval for any housing project. The County Planning Commission has given their approval of the project and these are the folks who go into the nuts and bolts of any project before them. I urge you to accept the recommendations of your professionals and let's get housing off the ground. thank you.
